means: The line layer alone - outlines with no colour underneath. On danbooru it is a binary page attribute: the image IS lines only.
does: Danbooru grammar, not description. It removes the fills, so every colour tag elsewhere in the prompt is contradicted and the frame goes black-on-white. This is the clearest contradiction case in the style set: 'lineart' next to 'teal soccer jersey, orange trim, number 7' asks for two incompatible pictures, and you get an unstable one rather than a compromise. Note the difference between the bare attribute and the MODIFIER forms - 'thick lineart', 'clean lineart', 'colored lineart' describe the line while leaving the fill alone, and those are what the line_weight card is built from.
reach_for_it: title cards, ending-sequence stills, a deliberately un-inked beat. If you only want to describe the LINE and still want a coloured frame, use a modifier form instead of the bare tag.
used_in: the modifier form throughout anime.draw.line_weight ('clean lineart, even line weight'); the bare attribute is in no current film
example_base: 1boy, solo, male focus, short black hair, dark jacket, standing on a rooftop, city skyline behind, late afternoon sun, looking away, masterpiece, best quality, very aesthetic, absurdres
read_it_as: Compare the SHADING, colour and line - not the pose or framing. Adding any clause re-rolls the model's conditioning, so composition moves between the two panels even at a fixed seed. An img2img pass from one fixed base image would isolate the tag properly; that is not built yet.
